headline: PSX books a fourth straight losing session as the Strait-of-Hormuz standoff overrides OGDC's record results.
summary: PSX booked a fourth straight losing session, closing at 172,642.16 (-993.91 pts, -0.57%), as the US-Iran standoff near the Strait of Hormuz keeps Brent near $98 and global risk appetite soft. OGDC posted a record Rs242.4bn profit and a record Rs17/share dividend, yet got sold off anyway — proof the tape is trading fear, not fundamentals, right now. August CPI held at 11.1% YoY and SBP is widely expected to hold rates on September 14, keeping bank carry trades intact. The desk's read: banks sitting on government paper remain the one qualified favoured pocket, E&P looks cheap but is not immune to the selling, and cyclicals stay off the table until the geopolitical overhang eases.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: UBL, HBL, MCB and BAHL all screen cheap (P/E 6-8x) with covered dividend yields near 7-10%, and the 6M T-bill (11.90%) / 10Y PIB (12.30%) carry stays intact with SBP expected to hold at 11.5% on Sept 14 (87.5% survey consensus) — a case for buying on broad-tape weakness, not for chasing the 4th down day.

sectors.name: Oil & Gas E&P
sectors.why: OGDC just posted a record Rs242.4bn net profit (+43% YoY, EPS Rs56.35) and a record Rs17/share dividend, and OGDC (P/E 5.69), PPL (P/E 7.7) and MARI (P/E 9.14) all screen cheap-to-fair on cash generation — but OGDC and PPL were still sold off in the Sept 7 session despite the results, so higher oil is helping the books, not the share prices, for now.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: Squeezed between volatile pump prices (diesel +Rs3.74/litre on Sept 5) and rising import costs while Brent sits near a seven-week high.

sectors.name: Autos, cement & power/IPPs
sectors.why: Rate-sensitive and import-cost exposed, with power/IPPs carrying the added overhang of unresolved circular debt heading into the IMF's still-unscheduled September review.

sectors.name: Small/thinly-capitalized banks & leveraged cyclicals
sectors.why: The confirmed 11.1% CPI print plus a hawkish hold-or-hike consensus at the Sept 14 MPC leaves no near-term rate-relief thesis for the weaker balance sheets.

watchlist.angle: The lowvol_pullback strategy is triggering now — on MUREB's own history it won 67% over 18 trades (+0.77% net/trade, still profitable out-of-sample at 60%). It's also the one live signal with a supportive fundamental read: fair P/E 7.31, healthy 11% net margin, moderate 4.49% dividend on a 33% payout.
watchlist.risk: Low-confidence backtest (n=18) and no dated catalyst on the calendar — a broad-tape flush would swamp a thin technical edge.

watchlist.angle: The vol_dryup_surge strategy is triggering now (65% hit rate over 17 trades, +0.99% net/trade, 75% out-of-sample) and NICL reports results tomorrow (2026-09-09, unconfirmed date) — a genuine near-term catalyst stacking on the technical trigger.
watchlist.risk: Fundamental read is 'caution' — P/E 14.21 is in the priciest third of PSX names, so a soft results print has little valuation cushion.

watchlist.angle: The rs_leader (relative-strength) strategy is triggering now (60% hit rate over 10 trades, +0.76% net/trade) and IPAK reports results in two sessions (2026-09-10, unconfirmed date).
watchlist.risk: Fundamental read is 'caution' — thin 7% net margin and a small 1.47% dividend give it little support if the results disappoint or the market keeps selling indiscriminately.

watchlist.angle: The desk's strongest live technical trigger — adx_trend_long has won 58% over 31 trades (+1.76% net/trade), still profitable out-of-sample at 62.5%, medium confidence, 15 sessions held.
watchlist.risk: Purely a momentum case: fundamentals are 'caution' (currently lossmaking, no dividend, beta 1.31), and there's no dated catalyst — a risk-off reversal would hit a name with this little fundamental cushion hardest.

catalysts.event: SBP MPC decision — 87.5% survey consensus expects a hold at 11.5%
Next PIB auction, Rs450bn target — watch whether long-end yields keep grinding higher

risks: Iran is reportedly finalizing a maritime exclusion zone near the Strait of Hormuz and Strait traffic is at its lowest since May — Brent is near a seven-week high ($98.13) and a further supply shock would hit the rupee and the import bill directly.
August CPI came in at 11.1% YoY, more than triple August 2025's print — persistent inflation caps the odds of any near-term rate relief that would help cyclicals re-rate.

Three of today's four live proven-strategy triggers (TPLT, NICL, IPAK) carry a 'caution' fundamental rating — technical momentum without a valuation or balance-sheet cushion is exactly what a risk-off tape tends to punish hardest.
